A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpaCE-10 and contain readable main text, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. Visual inspection resolves the heatmap content omitted by text extraction, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLLM evaluations, human performance, capability analyses, and an annotation-pipeline ablation in Table 7.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, including added SpaceVLM comparisons, human scores, capability analyses, and the retained pipeline ablation.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same hierarchical annotation pipeline: keyframe selection, GPT-4o captioning and inspection, structured extraction, human verification, and cross-capability integration. No proposed algorithm or component changes.

E1.justification: Both retain the same four indoor-scene sources, 811 scenes, eight QA types, and ten atomic capabilities. Image and point-cloud inputs and both question formats remain evaluated; multiple-choice coverage persists in Tables 3 and 6 despite Table 2's changed focus.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 6 add SpaceOm, SpaceQwen, and SpaceThinker-Qwen2.5VL-3B. They remove InternLM-XComposer2.5-7B, CogVLM2-LLaMA3-Chat-19B, Cambrian-13B, Cambrian-34B, and VILA1.5-40B. These additions and removals substantially revise the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes from combining single- and multiple-choice accuracies to a single-choice leaderboard with explicit unequal task weights, such as EQ ×0.09 and EP ×0.20. This substantially changes the headline evaluation and aggregation. Section 4.1 and the 3,091 single-choice/970 multiple-choice counts remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.3 and Figure 6 extend the existing atomic-capability analysis to all tested models, while Figure 4 broadens its representative selection. The basic-versus-compositional comparison design, pipeline-component ablation, and two qualitative QA case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both average the scores of two humans and retain the same statistical reporting practices. Neither reports model seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard errors, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 and 6 and Figure 4 contain extensive score and ranking revisions, alongside added SpaceVLM and Figure 6 results. Table 2's human/GPT-4o scores change from 72.0/37.4 to 81.5/49.0 under its changed evaluation, so these are not comparable performance gains. Table 6's Qwen2.5-VL-32B multiple/single ratio changes from 0.69 to 0.36, and Table 4's compositional EP average changes from 18.6% to 31.3%.

T1.justification: The task and capability definitions in Appendix A and their mapping in Table 5 are unchanged. Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark and annotation-pipeline contributions, the claim that MLLMs substantially trail humans, and the counting-bottleneck claim. Revised supporting scores do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds a Qwen-specific qualification to the interpretation that larger models resist question-format overfitting, acknowledging the opposite scaling tendency in this family. The pipeline explanations, 2D-versus-3D interpretation, and Section 5's annotation and indoor-scene limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: A new footnote beneath Table 2 identifies RemyxAI's SpaceVLM series and provides a model repository address. Existing benchmark/code access information, A100 hardware disclosure, evaluation framework, answer judging, and annotation implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The CogVLM and InternLM-XComposer references are removed, and Table 2 adds attribution to RemyxAI for SpaceVLMs. The related-work narrative and broader novelty positioning remain unchanged after matching renumbered references.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to results prose, capability-label capitalization, and the short new Appendix B.3. The introduction, methodology, definitions, limitations, conclusion, and case-study narrative remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with more model rows and a revised color scale, and Figure 6 adds a full-model heatmap. Tables 2, 3, and 6 revise headers, column ordering, or model grouping. Existing case-study figures are relocated and renumbered from Figures 6–8 to 7–9; the overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: Explicit weighting and broader model diagnostics are useful, but v2 introduces reporting inconsistencies. Appendix B.1 matched v1 Table 6's Qwen2.5-VL-32B ratio of 0.69; it retains that claim while v2's table reports 0.36. New Figure 6 conflicts with Figure 4 on LLaVA-OneVision-72B's C4 score, showing 44.1 versus 67.9. Table 4 also incorrectly reports 83.0 minus 42.8 as a 42.9-point drop. These issues outweigh the limited additions, while the benchmark design and core contributions remain intact.
